# MWCC (mwccpsp 3.0.1 build 219, -O4,p -sdatathreshold 0) codegen notes for Hot Shots Tennis: Get a Grip

Verified findings only: each line names the function where it was proven. Matching agents read this first
and append new verified findings (one `cat >> docs/MWCC-NOTES.md` per finding, never rewriting the file).

## Source shape
- The game is C++ with MSL-style containers. Empty variadic stubs are C++ `extern "C" void f(...)` (0x8822c).
- Ghidra often inverts if/else; try both orders (0x17dab8).
- Ghidra drops parentheses on non-associative float chains: `a * b * c` may be `a * (b * c)` (0x17dab8).
- Ghidra prints a signed `x / 2^k` as `if (x < 0) x = x + (2^k-1); ... x >> k`; only `x / 2^k` gives retail's
  bgez/sra/addiu/sra (0xee44c).
- Ghidra hoists repeated subexpressions (index products) into temporaries the source wrote inline (0xee44c).
- Ghidra turns `for (...) { if (hit) { r = i; break; } } return r;` into early returns; the break form
  matches (0x2535f0).
- Struct member access compiles like char-pointer arithmetic, not integer arithmetic: an int-typed base
  with `(base + i*4 + 0x3c)` gives different operand order; `self->items[i]` (or `char *` base with
  `base + 0x3c + i*4`) matches (0x2535f0).
- A global used as a struct base must be a pointer: with an int global, offsets > 0x7fff compile to
  `addiu 0x7fff` + rest (and unaligned swl/swr); retail is lui/addu with a negative offset (0x22c15c, 0x22c4ac).
- Module addresses Ghidra prints as numbers (`(T *)0x34179c`, `FUN(0x30fe20)`) are symbol addresses in
  retail: lui/addiu %hi/%lo, never lui/ori. Use `&DAT_0034179c` (0x1b5594). For `index + 0x338b58`
  write the base first: `(int)&DAT_00338b58 + index` (0xee44c).
- Calls passing a float to a callee without a prototype promote it to double (`__extendsfdf2`); give the
  callee a prototype with `float` parameters (0x97110).

## Frame / stack
- A 16-byte stack slot appears for: an empty allocator class passed by value to a non-inline function; an
  allocator temporary used as `Alloc().allocate(n)`; an address-taken local (e.g. `size` bound to a
  `const&` in a `less<>` functor call). Empty temporaries inside inline functions are optimised away.
- Address-taken locals are laid out in declaration order from the frame top; sorting Ghidra's
  `local_N`/`uStack_N` declarations by N ascending fixes many mismatches.
- `std::max` returning `const&` puts its operands on the stack; `const int&` locals avoid constant folding.
- A by-value char-member struct reaching the callee as `f.v` produces `move v0,zero; andi v0,0xff; seb`.
- Small structs are copied with lwc1/swc1 when passed/returned by value.

## Registers / branches
- `x < y` as the FIRST operand of `||` is computed into a register (`sltu v0/v1; bnez`); written as
  `y > x` or `y <= x` it compiles to `sltu at; bnez at`. A single `if (a < b)` uses `sltu at; beqz at`;
  `if (a >= b)` goes through a register (0xd8c98). A `greater`-style functor `Greater()(n, cap)` instead of
  `Less()(cap, n)` kept the functor's frame slot and fixed the register.
- Branch-likely with a store in the delay slot comes from both paths merging into one store:
  `T *mem = new(...); if (mem) mem = ctor(mem, ...); T *o = mem;` (0x134414); ternary and if/else forms
  stay 2 words off.
- A constructor writing through a local copy of `this` (`L *self = this; self->a = 0; ...`) stops MWCC
  folding `&y.b` into one offset (0x2291cc).

## Pragmas (allowed per file)
- `#pragma opt_strength_reduction off` when retail recomputes `base + i*k` instead of walking a pointer.
- `#pragma inline_depth(8)` for deep inline chains (container code).

## Runtime symbols (in symbols/EBOOT.BIN.txt)
- operator new 0xbcc `__nw__FUi`, delete 0xa00 `__dl__FPv`, delete[] 0x9e4 `__dla__FPv`, `__getreent` 0xfe3c
  (stderr at +0xc), fprintf 0xf3e8, abort 0xd518, length_error thrower 0x43b4, memmove 0x11090
  (`FUN_00011090`), memset 0x114c0 (`FUN_000114c0`).

## Virtual dispatch only comes out as `lw t9` in C++
A C function-pointer call through a vtable slot compiles to `lw v0,slot(a0); jalr v0`; retail's
`lw t9,0(a0); lw t9,slot(t9); jalr t9` is C++ virtual dispatch. This build's vtable has TWO
header slots before the first virtual, so a call to vtable offset 0x1c is the SIXTH declared
virtual (index 5), 0x24 is index 7, 0x34 index 11, 0x58 index 20, 0x9c index 37. Declare only the
explicit parameters -- `this` is implicit, and extra explicit args show up as extra `move aN`
arguments that retail does not have.
## Reusing the variable as a ternary result keeps it in the call's return register
`*(int *)(p + 0x564) = v != 0 ? FUN_00218c00(v) : 0;` makes MWCC sink the store into the zero path
(`beqzl v0, after; sw v0,off`). Writing it as
    if (v != 0)
        v = FUN_00218c00(v);
    *(int *)(p + 0x564) = v;
gives retail's shape: `beqzl v0, store; sw v0,off; jal; move a0,v0; store` -- the result variable
is coalesced with the callee's return register, so no `move` appears. Assigning the same ternary to
a fresh local instead costs a copy (`move v1,v0`) and one extra word.
## `% 2` on a 15-bit field keeps the signed-remainder fix-up
`((seed >> 16) & 0x7fff) % 2` compiles to `ext v0,v1,16,15; bgez v0,end; andi a3,v0,1; ...;
addiu a3,a3,-2`, i.e. the sign-fixing arm is dead but still emitted. Writing `& 1` instead drops
the whole `beqz`/`addiu` pair and the function no longer matches.
## Argument setup that differs only in order
When two `addiu aN,sp,off` argument setups come out swapped, the difference is the order MWCC's
scheduler emitted them in for the same call; the call itself is exact. Nothing in the source
changes it in the handful of cases seen here (0x001ca4a8's `FUN_00022434(t, param_1 + 0xa0, v)`).

- (lane fm6, unreviewed by the main session)
When two `addiu aN,sp,off` argument setups come out swapped, the order is decided by the argument's
TYPE, not by the statement order. 0x001ca4a8's `FUN_00022434(t, param_1 + 0xa0, v)` emitted
`addiu a1,s0,160` before `addiu a0,sp,32`; retail has a0 first. Declaring the callee as
`(float *, float *, float *)` and spelling the argument `(float *)((char *)param_1 + 0xa0)` flips
the order and the function becomes EXACT (89/89). The same argument cast straight from an int
pointer (`(float *)(param_1 + 0xa0)`) does NOT flip it, and neither does an `int` middle parameter,
so the byte cast is the part that matters: MWCC evaluates a `char *`-derived address before the
stack slot it already has, an int-typed expression after it.
## Offsets above 0x7fff need the byte cast
`*(int *)(param_1 + 0x8190)` (int parameter, int offset) makes MWCC form `addiu vN,sN,32767` and
then use UNALIGNED access pairs (`lwr`/`lwl`, `swr`/`swl`) for every field, because 0x8000 does not
fit a signed 16-bit addiu. The retail form is `lui v0,0x1; addu v0,s0,v0; sw zero,-32368(v0)` --
one clean `sw` per field, base rebuilt per access. Writing the same fields as
`*(int *)((char *)param_1 + 0x8190)` (or making the parameter itself `char *`) produces exactly
that, including the per-access `lui`/`addu` (0x001ef2ec, exact; 0x001f20d8). The byte cast also
keeps two adjacent zero stores from being merged into an `swr`/`swl` pair.
## Arm layout: identical chain, arms inline vs out of line
0x001f20d8's `if (n == 2) ... else if (n == 1) ... else if (n == 0) ...` comes out as retail's
`beql a0,2` / `beql a0,1` / `beqzl a0` / `b end` chain (every arm out of line) only when the
comparison is a `switch`-like chain; our build inlines the first arm and branches around it
(`bnel a0,v0,skip`), and a real `switch (n)` emits the chain in ascending case order (0,1,2)
rather than retail's descending 2,1,0. That layout difference is the whole remaining delta of
that function (100/99 words, 62 differ); it is a scheduler choice, not a source shape.
## `hstdiff` shows the last compiled object, not the current source
`tools/hstdiff.py` only disassembles `build/<module>/<dir>__<stem>/text.bin` next to the retail
bytes; it never compiles. An edited `wip/` file therefore diffs its OLD object and the diff looks
unchanged. Always run `python tools/hstmatch.py <file>` first, then `hstdiff` for the instruction
detail. A file with no `text.bin` at all (a fresh name) diffs as an empty left column, which reads
like a total mismatch rather than "not compiled yet".

## 2026-10-23 - 0x000ba78c: delete loops need each guard twice, and an `else` between them costs 2 words
A `for` loop releasing two slot arrays (`p = <field>; if (p != 0) delete p;`) only reaches retail's word count
when the null test is written twice: `if (p != 0) { if (p != 0) { delete p; slot = 0; } }`. Retail's slot block
holds three tests (outer guard, redundant guard, delete's own inline test) and MWCC folds a lone guard away
(116 words vs 120, 81 words differing). Writing the second field's load once after the first block instead of
inside an `if/else` pair is what shares the reload: with an `else` MWCC sinks a private `lw` into the first
branch's delay slot (2 words differ at the redundant-guard branch); without it, the reload is a single join
site and the redundant guard becomes `beqz` + `nop` targeting it. The redundant guard is harmless here since
its body is null-tested again.

the HIGHEST-address body. Retail here compares 0x18,0x12,0xc,0xb,0xa,0xe,0x14,8,0 and puts case 0's body at the
lowest address, so the source must list `case 0`, `case 8`, `case 0x14`, `case 0xe`, ... `case 0x18` - writing

## Address-split trap (2026-10-24)
A `lui 0x35` paired with a negative low half such as `-22828` addresses **0x34A6D4**, not 0x35A6D4, under mwcc's `(addr + 0x8000) >> 16` split. Reading the `lui` immediate as the base is wrong; retyping symbols on that reading cost 0x0023fad8 five differing words (196 -> 201) before it was reverted. Derive the base from `(hi << 16) + (int16)lo` instead.
## FPR round-trip lever (2026-10-24)
Holding integer values (keys, pointers, counts) as `float` locals taken from the bit pattern (`float f = *(float *)&x;`) and re-reading them as ints (`*(int *)&f`) forces mwcc to emit `sw`/`lwc1`/`swc1`/`lw` spill traffic instead of plain register moves. On 0x001c70c0 this added 13 words exactly where retail has them: 21 -> 34 of retail's 38.
## Disassembly vs source address space (2026-10-24)
`hstdis.py` prints **ram-address-space** addresses; source headers carry the file-space `data=` address. A constant shown at `0x2e8b38` lives at `0x002d8b38` — the offset is 0x10000 on this module. Reading the disassembly address as a source address yields nonsense bytes (at 0x2e8b38 you get `f4592e00 7a010000 01010101`; the real 12-byte PTMF at 0x2d8b38 is `{0, -1, 0x00102660}`).
## Declaration order sets frame slots (2026-10-24)
mwcc assigns stack slots in **local declaration order**, so a residue that shows a uniform +4/-4 offset across every `sp`-relative access is a declaration-order fault, not an opcode fault. On 0x002918f0 `char *local;` declared before `V tmp` put the spill at 28(sp) and the float triple at 16/20/24, while retail had the spill at 16 and the triple at 20/24/28; moving `V tmp = *(V *)v;` first shifted every access by +4 and closed all 8 differing words (57/57 -> EXACT, installed).
## When the FPR staging lever maps (2026-10-24)
Applies **only** when retail's `sw X,N(sp)` / `lwc1 $f,N(sp)` chains stage a **scalar the source controls** — a search key (0x001c70c0, 0x00103f74), an iterator pointer (0x00103f74), or a scalar carried into a call.
Does **not** map, and must be skipped without a compile, when the chains are:
1. **genuine float arithmetic against rodata** — lwc1 from a global base plus swc1 of the same register (0x00102490, where the 0x002d8b38 bytes are a 12-byte PTMF, not floats);
2. **`sw zero` vector/struct initialisation** — mwcc zeroes float aggregates with integer stores (pos_get_0027db5c, 16/20/24);
3. **a struct argument temp** — e.g. a 16-byte `Vec4` colour for an inlined `SetColor(Vec4)` (node_pair_create_000e59e4, 64-88);
4. **a struct-return copy** — a 12-byte `It` temporary copied field-by-field into its destination (container_find_index_0014c274, 48-56; six earlier shapes already disproved there).
Dose matters as much as mapping: on iterator code the **single-pointer** dose worked (0x00103f74 98 -> 105/105) while the full pair overshot (0x001c67e8 29 -> 43/44). Keep rule: **words improved OR differ improved OR EXACT**.

## CSE: address-level vs value-level (2026-10-24)
The cast trick (`*(int *)((char *)p + 0x50)`) defeats a CSE on a shared **address expression** — it converted 0x0008add8. It does **not** defeat a CSE on a loaded **value**: on 0x002a45d8 retail recomputes `lbu / addiu -4 / sltiu 2` for the same `(byte@+0x324 - 4) < 2` guard twice, and neither `(char *)DAT_003415a8 + 0x324` nor a `volatile unsigned char *` read made mwcc re-emit the trio — both measured identically at 214/216, 115 differ. Distinguish the two before spending a probe: if the shared thing is an address, re-spell it; if it is a loaded byte or a comparison on one, the source has no handle on the CSE.
## Frame-slot delta: cause vs consequence (2026-10-24)
A uniform sp-relative delta is only *actionable* when it is the **cause**: same frame size on both sides, the same number of distinct slots, and every paired access shifted by the same constant — i.e. one block of values sitting at different addresses. Check those three numbers before spending a compile (`try/lane-work/frameclass.py`). 0x002918f0 was this case and reordering declarations fixed it. When the delta is a **consequence** — frame size differs, or one side uses more distinct slots because it spilled a value the other kept in a register — no declaration permutation can move it; the 0x002a8fbc, state_dispatch pair and clamp_vec_reset trials all failed for that reason. Inventory result: of 10 remaining uniform-delta files, all 10 classify as cause by frame size and slot count, 4 have no declaration block to permute (0-1 locals at function scope), and the 6 with a real block (ctor_court_intro, ctor_regulation, ctor_main_result, game_slot_select, release_handles, vec_reserve_copy) took 5 permutations each — 30 compiles, **zero drops**. So the cause/consequence test is necessary but not sufficient: a genuine cause still only converts when the shifted block is the one whose order mwcc is choosing differently.
- Differ counts are not size-normalised: a variant that emits two fewer words can shed one "differing" word for free, because the comparison runs over a shorter stream. For any edit that changes instruction count, require the differ drop to exceed the size delta before calling it an alignment gain, or judge by the first-diff offset instead — 0x00267f24's entity retype moved differ 321 → 320 while dropping two words, i.e. indistinguishable from noise.
- **Keep/restore rule, final form.** A variant is an alignment gain only if the differing-word drop *exceeds* the size delta it introduced, measured in the direction of retail: for a file **under** retail the word count must rise (shortfall shrink) and for a file **over** retail it must fall, with the differ count judged net of that movement. Raw differ drops on size-changing edits are not evidence — a shorter stream has fewer words available to differ, so shedding one differing word per two words removed is arithmetic, not alignment. The sounder signal is the **first-diff offset**: a real alignment gain moves the first divergence later even when the counts move little.
- **By-value aggregate lever (established on 0x00203680).** A stack home is a consequence of where the ABI puts a value, never something the source can request. Routing an aggregate through `static inline T holdX(T v) { return v; }` and using `T q = holdX(*p);` makes the compiler give the copy a callee-owned home, producing the `lwc1`/`swc1` staging retail has: on quad_project this moved **70 → 83/155 words, differ 153 → 145** with the first diff moving from +0x0 to +0x4. The failed alternatives, all disproved on the same file, are instructive: `volatile T *q = &local` (folded, lost a word), scalar `$f20` liveness probes (re-materialised), and an argument-list shuffle (neutral). **Second application, six outputs:** wrapping `struct Proj { float a..f; }` through `holdProj` after the call that fills it by address moved **83 → 107/155**, differ 145 → 147 — a 24-word gain with a 2-word differ rise and the first diff moving back to +0x0. The lever bites for aggregates that *arrive* by value; for ones already given up by address it re-introduces a copy rather than recovering retail's placement, so use it for entry copies and returns, not for call outputs.
- **Output-array lever (measured once, does not transfer).** Spelling a group of address-taken outputs as `float out[N]` and passing `&out[0]`…`&out[N-1]` beat six separate scalars on **both** metrics on 0x00203680: 83/155 words differ 145 → **82/155 differ 143**, first diff unchanged at +0x4. Do not re-run this sweep without new input: the idiom is essentially unique to quad_project in this tree.
- **Symmetric-vs-steep test for register residues (use before any permutation).** From a file's paired listing, extract the register appearing on each side of every differing row and build the map ours→retail. If the map is a bijection whose counts match (`co[a] == cr[b]` for every pair), the exchange is a **symmetric pair** — two equally good candidates that the allocator picked differently — and no declaration permutation can steer it; do not spend compiles. If one register carries a clearly longer live range (count spread >= 2) the assignment is **steeply ranked** and ordering *may* steer it. Use this test to skip symmetric files outright, not to promise that steep ones will convert.

2026-10-26 (lane wf20261026b-e01-01, research; toys try/lane-work/probes/b1-b9.c): MWCC's callee-saved order is the Chaitin SIMPLIFY order, not use count, loop depth, calls spanned or live-range length. Virtual registers are visited in pseudo order (scalar parameters in declaration order, then locals in DECLARATION order - not definition order - then compiler temps); every node whose degree is below K is pushed in that pass; the stack is coloured in reverse with the lowest free s-register. So values pushed in the same pass get earlier-declared = higher s-reg, but a value that interferes with >= 6 other virtual registers (any mix of one-instruction temps such as `lui` address halves and other call-crossing locals; the threshold moved exactly one step per extra neighbour) misses the first pass and takes a LOWER s-reg than every first-pass value, whatever its declaration position (temps in a stretch where only `a` is live flip a/b; the same temps where both are live do not). When both values are heavy, declaration order returns. 11 uses of a parameter, a use inside a loop, 3 extra calls of life and 5 extra uses as call arguments never moved it. Practical lever: what flips a pair is WHICH value carries the short temporaries during its life (an expression evaluated while only one of them is live), not how often it is used.

## Pass 17 (2026-10-28) - sweep lessons
- **Hoisted preheader loads follow statement order, and body-local declarations are NOT hoisted by this MWCC.** When a
  loop-invariant load must sit between the guard's count load and the branch (`lw count; lw colour; blez count`), you
  cannot get it there by declaring it inside the body: the load stays in the body and costs 2 extra words (0x5a500:
  9 -> 14 differ). Only a statement before the loop hoists, and then it always precedes the guard load.
- **Compare encoding is coupled to arm layout.** `c.ngt.s` is what the "mirrored" spelling (`const > x`, trunc arm as
  the then-block) emits; `c.le.s` only appears when the fixup test is written positively (`const <= x` fixup-then or as
  an early-return guard), and those put the fixup arm inline: +32 to +36 words. Do not spend a pass trying to convert
  the encoding without accepting the layout; treat a lone `c.ngt.s`/`c.le.s` residual as a measured wall.
- **`addu` operand order is source order, but index 0 canonicalises differently.** `base + off + k` vs `off + base + k`
  flips the operand order; a store at offset 0 written as the plain pointer-index form (`base + off`, no `+ 0`) keeps
  the base-first order while stores 1..3 want offset-first. Split the spelling per store instead of for the whole run.
- **Copy-through-temp fixes FP load order in a lerp.** `float cur = r->f0; r->f0 = cur + k * (r->f8 - cur);` makes MWCC
  load the current corner before the target, matching retail's `lwc1` order (0x622d4: 6 -> 2 differ).
- **Frame home area is not reachable from the call site.** Neither an unprototyped function-pointer call (`void (*)()`)
  nor a variadic one (`void (*)(void *, ...)`) reserves the 16 bytes: both keep the smaller frame. A word-extent match
  can coexist with a 16-byte frame deficit because sp-relative offsets do not shift; the frame is one differing word,
  not a shifter.
- **C++ virtual-call shape:** `lw t9,0(a0); lw t9,N(t9); jalr t9` = vtable pointer at offset 0 of the object, `this`
  kept in a0, slot at +N. Plain C struct-of-function-pointers calls through the object base register into v0 instead
  (`lw v0,0(s5); lw v0,N(v0); jalr v0`), which is a 2-3 word difference per dispatch.
## Pass 18 (2026-10-28)
- **A live argument register forces the address temp into t0.** If retail computes an address with `sll t0,...` where
  you get `sll a0,...` (and the surrounding code matches), an argument register is still live at that point: the
  following call takes MORE parameters than you declared. `0x622d4` needed `FUN_000790d0(idx, w, h, fade)` - with all
  four passed, a0-a3 stay live, the index*24 temp moves to t0, and the function goes EXACT. Diagnostic rule: count the
  a-registers that retail never clobbers between entry and the call, and declare that many parameters.
- **Local-area alignment is not reachable.** `__attribute__((aligned(16)))` compiles and is ignored;
  `__declspec(align(16))` does not compile at all. A local area that retail starts at a 16-byte boundary (sp+64 instead
  of sp+48) is therefore a frame you cannot reproduce by aligning the array.
- **Unused locals are eliminated before frame layout**, so a dummy array cannot pad a frame hole - but the frame does
  follow declaration order, with the LAST-declared local lowest (`0x4c66c`: four orders tried, all -320).
- A `c.le.s`/`c.ngt.s` residual is not convertible by negating the source either: `!(const > x)` flipped the arm
  layout and gave 40 differing words on `0x6dc58` (vs 4 for the kept spelling).

The diagnostic is: **if retail keeps a value live that you do not, ask whether it is an outgoing argument.** It
converted `0x622d4`. Applied to the rest, all five are non-argument causes, each verified against the call sites:
- `0x6bd24` (1 differ): the disputed `sw s5,40(sp)` is the dead half of an 8-byte local at sp+40/44 - retail reads
  sp+44 back (`lw v1,44(sp)`, copied to two places) and finally `lw a0,44(sp)` into `operator delete`. Arity of every
  call checked (new 1, 0xfe3c 0, 0xf3e8 2, 0xd518 0, self 4, delete 1). Not arguments; it needs the 8-byte object form.
- `0x4f130` (2): `lui a1,0x2` vs `move a1,v0` is constant CSE with the hi half of the `o->f1a0b0` address, which retail
  decomposes as `o + 0x20000 - 24400`. The call already passes 5 args (a0-a3 + t0). Not arguments.
- `0x494d0` (2): retail's `jal` delay slot holds the *following* store, ours holds the argument move; both set a0-a2.
  A delay-slot scheduling tie, not arity.
- `0x44550` (2): `0x51478(handle, tag)` really takes only two arguments - the f0-f3 loads before it feed the
  subtractions that compute f22/f24, and `0x524a8` gets 8 float args + 1 stack arg in both builds. FP liveness.
- `0x6b6f8` (50): all eight calls' arities match; the sp+40 object is a 12-byte local (`{1, a1, ?, a1}`) passed by
  address to `0x6bd24`. Allocation.
- `0x180c` (15): single call `0x2110(&tmp)`; residual is the 8-word header copy using one temp (v0, sequential) in
  retail vs two interleaved temps here.
- `0x4c8d8` (88): leaf, no calls - the diagnostic does not apply.
Rule of thumb from the sweep: a live-argument problem shows as a *scratch temp in a0..a3 where retail uses t0..t3*
and, at the same time, an a-register that retail never clobbers. Anything else (dead half of a local, constant CSE,
delay-slot filler, FP liveness) is not an arity problem and should be capped quickly.

## 16-byte-aligned stack temporaries, and breaking address CSE
Two mechanisms measured on `0x00141718` (2026-10-28):
**`__attribute__((aligned(16)))` on a typedef works; between `struct` and the tag it does not.**
`struct __attribute__((aligned(16))) Item { ... };` is a hard "illegal struct/union/enum/class
definition" in mwccpsp 2.1.9, but `typedef struct { ... } __attribute__((aligned(16))) Item;` compiles
and gives the type 16-byte alignment. The alignment is what decides where mwcc puts a 48-byte temp:
unaligned it lands at `sp+48`, aligned it lands at `sp+32` (the bottom of the local area, straight after
the save block), which is where retail keeps it. Every offset in a body that copies through such a temp
is wrong until this is right, so it looks like a 40-word diff and is really one declaration.
**An address argument that retail recomputes must not be CSE-able.**
When retail emits `addiu a0,s4,2284` twice for the same sub-object but the source passes the same
expression twice, mwcc keeps it in a saved register (`addiu s0,s3,2284`) and the whole register
allocation shifts. Giving the two calls different *types* for the same address — `self + 0x8ec` as
`char *` for one, `(int)(self + 0x8ec)` for the other — stops the CSE and restores the two `addiu a0`
forms. Declaring the containing object properly (`struct Big { char pad[0x8e0]; Arr arr; }` with `self`
of that type) is the cleaner fix for the *offsets*, since every member access then folds to `offset(s4)`.
## The parked word-count ties are not flag-reachable (measured 2026-10-28)
Pile: the 9 of 69 NEARs whose recorded body length already equals retail's — the colour/layout
class. Tool: `tools/flagmatrix.py` (runs the real matcher per variant; a hit would be byte-equality).
Baseline differ counts in brackets:
`0x000d99b8` (10), `0x001a5a1c` (12), `0x00199904` (14), `0x001aecf4` (15), `0x0015a728` (17),
`0x001c38e0` (23), `0x00171588` (29), `0x00285d04` (30), `0x000e5580` (47).
Variants tried inside build 219 — every one of the nine stayed MISMATCH:
| variant | flags | best-of-nine result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| profile | `-O4,p -sdatathreshold 0` | **minimum for all nine** |
| O3p | `-O3,p` | equals profile on 7, worse on `0x00285d04` (61 vs 30) |
| O4s | `-O4,s` | worse on 3 (`0x001c38e0` 49, `0x00199904` 35, `0x000e5580` 47) |
| O2p | `-O2,p` | worse on all (12→70, 23→67, 29→70 …) |
| L3nospeed | `-O3` | worse on 3 |
| L4nospeed | `-O4` | no improvement |
| lvl3speed | `-opt level=3,speed` | no improvement |
| O4pnoin | `-O4,p -opt nointrinsics` | identical to profile |
| O4pinauto / O4pinl2 / O4pbottomup | `-inline auto / level=2 / bottomup` | identical to profile |
| strictenum / enumint | `-strict on -enum int` | identical to profile |
Two control runs with other compiler builds at the profile flags (`210`, `205`) also fail all nine.
Those are diagnostic only: the retail profile is build 219, and a match from another build would be a
false match for the rest of the object.
**The help exposes no further knobs that could move allocation:** no aliasing/strict-aliasing option,
no `-proc`/`-mcpu`/`-march`, no alignment flag, no scheduler switch (`-opt level=3` is what turns
scheduling on, and it is already the profile). Alignment is reachable only at source level
(`__attribute__((aligned(16)))`, see the section above) — that is the one lever this matrix cannot pull.
**Conclusion:** the nine word-count ties are unreachable by flag variation with this toolchain
profile. Any further progress on that class has to come from the source shape (declaration order,
address-taking, aggregate types), not from the build.

- A frame that is 16 bytes larger than `round16(locals + 4*saves)` with nothing referencing the extra
  words (no `addiu aN,sp,M`, no store) is one elided by-value aggregate/allocator temporary in the
  frame-top local region, shared by every such temporary in the function. Tested at `0x0017b554`
  (2026-10-28): passing a by-value EMPTY class to the teardown calls gives retail's 48-byte frame but
  adds `move v0,zero; seb aN,v0` per call, and a 4-byte class makes the temp addressable
  (`lw aN,0(sM)`, frame +16 more); retail's plain `move aN,zero` therefore means the slot came from an
  inline allocator form (`Alloc().allocate(n)`), which reserves the slot and emits no argument code.
  An inline function *returning* the empty tag (`MakeAlloc()`) does NOT: the return value becomes an
  addressable temp and the frame grows to 64 bytes (measured on `0x0017b554`, 2026-10-28).
  Nor does ANY dead local: on `0x0027eedc` (2026-10-28) five forms all compiled to the identical
  frame - `__attribute__((aligned(16))) char pad[16]`, plain `char pad[16]`, an unused
  `union { double; int[2]; }`, an address-taken int whose address is dead, and a 16-byte aggregate
  passed by value to a `static inline` no-op. Unused locals are stripped and an inline callee's
  by-value temp is elided WITH its slot. The slot survives only when the aggregate crosses an
  OUT-OF-LINE call boundary; a body whose calls have no tag position cannot be given it.
  A loop-invariant `base + K` address used both inside an inner loop and after it is hoisted into a
  saved register (one extra save); rewriting one use as pointer arithmetic (`(int)(p + K)` vs
  `(int)p + K`) does NOT stop it - the two spellings compile to identical bytes.
- An `||` guard chain that returns a constant (`if (p == 0 || byte == 0) return 1; return 0;`) compiles
  to a folded branch chain with an extra `xor/sltiu` bool. Writing it as the INVERTED nest —
  `if (p != 0) { if (byte != 0) { return 0; } } return 1;`, one statement per operand, surviving return
  last — reproduces retail's `beqzl p` + `li v0,1` delay, `beqz byte` + `b <return>` with
  `move v0,zero` in the delay (0x000fb5f4: 78/80 words 66 differ -> 80/80 words 44 differ,
  2026-10-28). Splitting into two positive `if (...) return 1;` statements regresses (77/80, 72 differ),
  so the polarity of the nest is what matters. The same trick does NOT transfer to a value chain of
  constant returns (`if (v == 11) return 1; if (v != 7) return 0;`): inverting it buys 2 differing
  words but loses one word of count, `else if` is byte-identical, and expressing it as `(v ^ K)`
  unsigned predicates XORed with 1 costs 4 words (0x000fb5f4, 2026-10-28). There mwcc chooses to
  place the constant-return block out of line (`beql`) where retail keeps it inline between the two
  tests (`bnel` + the next test's constant in the delay slot).
- A short-circuit `&&` chain used as a predicate narrows the result to a byte (`andi v0,v0,0xff`).

  the value directly: `t = (unsigned)(0 < (unsigned)n); if ((t ^ 1) == 0)` yields retail's

## Frame-first reconstruction (2026-10-28, pass 40; 0x000b8118, 0x00216c28)
Six earlier passes died at first diff +0x0 because the body was written before the stack frame. Get the frame
and the saved-register set right FIRST; both bodies below then reached retail's exact word count, at 1 and 11
differing words.
- **FRAME FIRST — MWCC gives the first-declared local the HIGH address.** 0x000b8118's 784-byte frame is
  16 bytes of saves + a 64-byte `M4` at sp+16 + a 704-byte `Big` at sp+80, and it reproduces only with `Big`
  declared BEFORE `M4`; the reverse puts `M4` at sp+720 and swaps the two ctor arguments. A frame 16 bytes too
  large with an extra `swc1 $fN` save means a float temp is live across a call — materialise it into the field
  the source stores it to instead (`big.f200 = f1; big.f214 = F(CONST*f1); self->f78 = CONST*G(&big);` with the
  store landing in the last call's delay slot).
- **Mirrored ternary arm order.** `(a != b) ? 1.0f : 0.0f` gives retail's `beql v1,v0` with `mtc1 zero,$f0` in
  the delay slot; `(a == b) ? 0.0f : 1.0f` gives the inverted `bnel` form plus one extra word (0x000b8118).
- **Signed `% 16`, not `& 15`.** The ring index in 0x00216c28 needs a signed modulo: `% 16` emits
  `bgez / andi / beqzl / sll / addiu -16 / sll`; `& 15` emits a bare `andi` and every later word shifts.
- **Re-derive a draft's global symbol addresses from the lui/addiu pair.** Two names written 0x10000 too high
  still linked and compiled to `lui 0x35` where retail has `lui 0x34` (0x003386b8 and 0x00338ac4, not
  0x003486b8 / 0x00348ac4).
- **Flag-byte width:** `unsigned char *self` gives `lbu`; `char *self` gives `lb` and word 0 differs (0x00216c28).
- **addu operand order is not source-fixable here:** 0x000b8118's single remaining word is retail
  `addu v0,v0,s0` (index first) against `addu v0,s0,v0`. `(k*24 + (char*)self)[34]`, an int-cast sum
  `(char*)(k*24 + (int)self) + 136`, `24 * k`, and an unsigned index all normalise back to pointer-first.
### Frame-first, continued (2026-10-28, pass 41; 0x000bd568, 0x0016aafc, 0x00190458)
- **A value used twice is what grows the frame.** 0x000bd568 is 48 bytes with four saves until `v = e->f0c + 20` is a local used BOTH as the record field `t.p` and as FUN_000bdb14's 6th argument; then it becomes retail's 64 with s3..s0. Same rule as the big-stack-object case: find the value retail keeps live across a call, not the declaration order.
- **FPR numbering: earlier-declared float local gets the HIGHER saved FPR.** 0x0016aafc needs `float y = b; float x = CONST * a;` to put x in f20 and y in f21; declaring x first swaps them and costs ~13 words.
- **`extern float fabsf(float);` is the abs.s intrinsic.** `<math.h>` is not on this lane's include path and `__builtin_fabsf` links as an external symbol.
- **Symbol names need EIGHT hex digits.** `FUN_000462a0`, not `FUN_00462a0`: the short form is reported as MISSING_SYMBOLS rather than relocating.
- **Assignment to a fresh float local does not stop in-place folding**: 0x0016aafc's second angle still becomes `mul.s f21,f21,f0` where retail has `mul.s f2,f0,f21` and keeps f21 raw, leaving a 4-word gap.

## Address decoding and stack-buffer assignment (2026-10-28, fresh reconstructions)
- **A `lui imm; addiu lo` pair sign-extends `lo`.** Decode it as `(imm << 16) + (int16)lo`, never
  `(imm << 16) | lo`. `lui 0x31; addiu -24836` is `0x00310000 - 0x6104 = 0x00309efc`, and
  `lui 0x31; addiu -28268` is `0x00309194` — both look like `0x0031....` if you read the hi half only.
  Writing `DAT_00319efc` produced `lui 0x32; addiu -24836`, a first diff at `+0x18` that masqueraded as
  a frame bug for two compiles (0x002ab5ac). Re-derive every address from the pair before blaming the frame.
- **Two stack buffers declared together are assigned by use at the call sites, not by declaration order.**
  Swapping the declarations of `r1[3]`/`r2[3]` changed nothing; swapping which array each call receives
  (and later swapping the declarations once the block sat outside the `if`) was what moved a buffer from
  `sp+36` to `sp+24`. If the offsets are reversed, change the arguments first, then the order.
- **A call group retail places after a null test must sit outside the `if`.** Putting
  `FUN_000031f0/FUN_00003e04/FUN_00190880/FUN_000462a0/FUN_00004138` inside `if (p != 0)` moved the
  `beqz` target 0x58 bytes and shifted every later word; hoisting them out restored the real branch range
  (0x002ab5ac).
- **`beqz v0,<exit>` with `move s1,v0` in the delay comes from the assignment inside the condition:**
  `if ((p = (int *)FUN_00000bcc(0x88)) == 0) goto L_after;`. Writing `p = FUN(...); if (p == 0) goto ...`
  gives `move s1,v0; beqz s1,<exit>` with a `nop` delay instead, and every later word shifts.
## Recipe: re-read the pointer for every store (2026-10-28, 0x0021b088 EXACT)
- **Hold the value, not the address.** When retail stores twice through the same object, write the
  pointer expression again for each store instead of caching it in a local:
  `((int *)p[0x64/4])[0x60/4] = 0;` … `((float *)p[0x64/4])[0x64/4] = f;`. One cached `q` produces one
  load and one store placement; two expressions produce retail's **double `lw v0,100(s2)`**, the zero
  store in the `beqz` delay and the `swc1` in the `jal` delay. This closed 0x0021b088 (80/80, EXACT)
  after nine compiles on which every other tail spelling stalled at 16 differing words.
- **The zero-initialised else value is free evidence.** `f = 0.0f; if (c) f = -16.0f;` before the store
  yields the unconditional `mtc1 zero,$f0` that sits *above* the branch in retail; a branch-local store
  never produces it.
- **Counter-example (frame cost): holding the value across a call inflates the frame.** The same draft
  with `FUN_00103480(...); *ptr = f;` (f live across the call) went to 82/80 words and 82 differ at
  `+0x0`, because the float joins the saved set. Store before the call and let the scheduler sink it
  into the delay slot instead.
- This is a **liveness rule, not a tail trick**: the same cause shows up as a store that will not sink
  into a delay slot, an argument materialised late (`move a0,s0` / `addiu a0,sp,24` in the `jal` delay),
  or one extra saved register. When a draft parks with any of those three symptoms, re-read the base
  expression per use before changing anything else.
## Correction: `addu` operand order IS source-controllable (2026-10-28, 0x000b8118 EXACT)
Earlier notes (line 17 table, and the 0x18f1ac entry) implied an `addu` operand mismatch could be a
canonicalisation wall. It is not. The two spellings differ and both are reachable:
| spelling | code |
| --- | --- |
| `*(float *)((char *)(24 * k + (int)self) + 136)` | `addu v0,s0,v0` (base first) |
| `*(float *)((char *)self + off + 136)` with `int off = k * 24` | `addu v0,s0,v0` |
| **`*(float *)((char *)((char *)self + 136) + off)`** | **`addu v0,v0,s0`** (offset accumulated into, base added last) |
The rule: put the **base pointer plus any constant** in its own cast expression, and add the integer
offset as the outermost `+`. `0x000b8118` sat at 78/78 words with only that rotation left and went
EXACT on this change alone; `0x000bd568` used the same form to flip its table read (there the base was
`self + 0x1dc`). When a draft's only residual is `addu vX,sN,vM` vs `addu vX,vM,sN`, rewrite the address
this way before parking it as canonicalisation.
## Where the retail bytes live, and how to read data (jump tables) from them
Do not search the filesystem for `EBOOT.BIN` — there is no such file. The matcher resolves the module
through its own cache:
```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "tools"); import hstmatch as H
data, seg = H.module_bytes({}, "EBOOT.BIN")     # data: the loaded image, seg: the PT_LOAD header
off = seg["file_offset"] + (0x002c0168 - seg["start"])
entry = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, off)[0]
```
The image is `<private tree>\hst-1009\hst-build\inputs\selected.elf` (path comes from
`revision-selection.json` + `ledger/campaign.json`, not from `hst-config.json`), and the address→offset
rule is `file_offset + (va - seg["start"])` with `start=0`, `file_offset=84` in this build.
Worked example (`0x000c13e0`, jump table at `0x002c0168`, 14 entries): only entries **4** and **9**
point at `0xc1420` (the state machine); the other twelve point at `0xc1414`, which is
`li v1,9; b end; sw v1,64(a0)` — so the switch is `if (st==4 || st==9) {…} else {field64 = 9;}`,
not fourteen distinct arms. Reading the table before writing a switch is cheap; guessing its layout is not.
## Branch-likely and delay-slot placement: what source cannot steer (measured 2026-10-28)
The residual class that stops every body at retail's exact word count is mwcc's choice of (a) which arm gets
`beql`/`bnel` and (b) which statement fills the delay slot. A bounded six-form sweep on `0x000dc6a4` (95/95
words, 46 differ, first at `+0x30`) measured every spelling the class suggests:
| form | words | differ | first diff |
| `if (mode != 1) { … }` outer, `if (mode == 0) { … }` inner | **95/95** | **46** | `+0x30` |
| `if (!mode)` instead of `if (mode == 0)` | 95/95 | 46 | `+0x30` (byte-identical) |
| `goto` label placed at the arm, arm as the label's block | 92/95 | 85 | `+0x14` |
| arms swapped, condition negated | 93/95 | 85 | `+0x14` |
| `mode == 0` test hoisted to function scope | 97/95 | 61 | `+0x14` |
| `default` arm last, chain 3/2/1/0 reordered | 93/95 | 87 | `+0x14` |
| (earlier) `switch` with cases 3/2/1/0 | 94/95 | 92 | `+0xc` |
Rules this establishes:
- `if (!x)` and `if (x == 0)` are **byte-identical**; never spend a compile distinguishing them.
- Writing the *then* block as a `goto` target, or swapping arms and negating, moves the first diff **backwards**
  (to `+0x14`), because mwcc then re-materialises the compare itself. The plain fall-through form is strictly best.
- A `switch` on the same values reorders the comparison chain (3,2,1 instead of 3,2,1,0) and loses 2 words.
- No source form makes mwcc emit a likely branch **into** an arm while sinking the previous statement into the
  other branch's delay slot (retail's `beqzl a1,<arm>` with the arm's first word in the delay). That is a
  block-layout decision, so bodies blocked on it park at their word count rather than chasing the placement.
Expect the same shape on `0x000fb5f4` (`+0x68`: retail `bnel a0,v0,<return>` with `move v0,zero` in the delay
against our `beql a0,v0,<arm>` + `b <return>`), `0x002872a0` and `0x000c13e0`; do not re-spend compiles on the
polarity of those chains either.
## The 16 untouched stack bytes: variadics tested and falsified (2026-10-28)
Two bodies reach retail's exact word count with the *only* difference being a frame that is 16 bytes larger in
retail while retail never touches those bytes: `0x000d3298` (ours 16 B / retail 32 B) and `0x0027eedc`
(ours 16 B / retail 32 B). Both had the same prologue otherwise: `ra,s2,s1,s0` at 12/8/4/0 and no other
`sp`-relative access anywhere in the body.
Hypothesis: a variadic definition (`int f(int a0, int a1, ...)`) reserves the incoming-argument save area
without storing to it. **Falsified on both bodies, and it cannot hold in principle**: mwccpsp *always* spills the
named-argument registers that varargs can read.
| body | spelling | frame | words | differ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x000d3298` | `int *f(int *p,int n)` | 16 | 95/95 | 62 |
| `0x000d3298` | `int *f(int *p,int n,...)` | **80** | 101/95 | 98 |
| `0x0027eedc` | `void f(int *p,uint n,int k)` | 16 | 92/92 | 70 |
| `0x0027eedc` | `void f(int *p,uint n,int k,...)` | **96** | 97/92 | 92 |
The variadic prologue stores `a2` at 56(sp) / `a3` at 60(sp) / `t0` at 64(sp) / `t1` at 68(sp) (and
`a3` at 76 / `t0` at 80 on the second body), so it both grows the frame past the target *and* adds exactly the
`sp` references retail lacks. Retail's prologue has no `a2+` stores at all, which rules out every varargs shape,
including a variadic tail on a later parameter.
One adjacent probe also closed: forcing a debug frame with `--flags "-c -O4,p -sdatathreshold 0 -g"` produces an
object `psp-ld` rejects as "file in wrong format" under this kit, so `-g` cannot be used to test a widened frame
here. With dead locals, by-value aggregates without a tag argument position, variadics and `-g` all excluded, the
16 untouched bytes stay an unexplained artifact of the original build rather than a reachable source shape; bodies
blocked on it are frame-only parks, and their bodies should be finished to retail's word count and left there.
2026-10-29 (0x0022c05c EXACT, lane dsn3, phase 3): a global-array short read whose offset does not fit a signed 16-bit displacement must be written as `((short *)((char *)DAT_xxx + 0xD4E6))[idx]` — casting the pointer past the constant and then indexing it. That gives retail's index-first `addu v1,v1,a0` and splits the offset into `lui 0x1` + `lh -0x2b1a` (0x10000 - 0x2B1A = 0xD4E6). Writing the address as `idx*2 + (int)DAT_xxx` plus the same constant costs one word: MWCC folds 0xD4E6 into 0x1D4E6 (lui 0x2) and emits `addu v1,a0,v1` (base first). A one-word addu-operand tie on a global table read is therefore a spelling fix, not canonicalisation.
2026-10-29 (0x000de208 + 0x000de238/0x000de268/0x000de298 EXACT, lane dsn3, phase 3): a guard pair whose two failures both branch to ONE trailing `jr ra` with no zero store is a single-expression short-circuit return, not two early returns. `return s->flag != 0 && (a1 < 0 || s->value == a1);` gives `lbu; sltu v0,zero,v0; beqz v0,<trailer>` then `slt v0,a1,zero; bnez v0,<trailer>` with the comparison body in the fall-through — retail reuses v0 (0 from the first test, the slt result from the second) as the return value, so the trailer needs no `move v0,zero`. Early-return spellings invert the guards and put the body out of line (13 words vs 12). The xor operand order follows the source: `s->value == a1` emits `xor v0,v0,a1`, `a1 == s->value` emits `xor v0,a1,v0` — the twin at 0x000de298 needs the latter.
2026-10-29 (0x00204400 EXACT, lane dsn3, phase 3): when a function's failure paths all branch to ONE trailing `move v0,zero`, write the guards as a nested form with a single final `return 0` — `if (p != 0) { if (i >= 0 && i < 15) return p + i*16; } return 0;` — not as a flat `if (a || b || c) return 0;` chain, which duplicates the zero block per failure and inverts the compares (`slti v0` + `bnezl` instead of retail's `slti at` + `beqz`). The tell is `slti at`: the compare result is branch-only, so the source must not use it as a value.
2026-10-29 (0x0022bf40 EXACT, lane dsn3, phase 3): a constant-trip (256) byte-fill whose retail body re-loads the base global and the constant each pass is `#pragma opt_strength_reduction off` + `#pragma opt_unroll_loops off`; either alone is not enough and without both mwcc emits 58-62 words instead of 13. With the pragmas the index-first cast `((unsigned char *)(i + (int)DAT_xxx))[0xc100]` gives retail's `addu a2,a3,a2` and splits +0xC100 into `lui 0x1` + `sb -0x3f00`.
## `(char *)0 +` seeds an int-first `addu`; write a split constant as ONE number (2026-10-28, 0x0022cb40, 0x0022cb04 EXACT)
Both are `... = G[d + 0x90D0 + a*384 + b*64 + c*8 + 0x3500]` (G = `unsigned char *DAT_003415a8`). Retail materialises
0x90D0 as `addiu v0,a3,0x7fff; addiu a3,v0,0x10d1` and adds the `a*384` term to the base FIRST (`addu v0,v0,a0`, dst =
the shift term). Two rules fell out:
- **Never pre-split the constant yourself.** Writing `d + 0x8CD0` (= `0x7fff + 0xcd1`) makes mwcc materialise
  `addiu ...,3281`; write the true total `d + 0x90D0` and mwcc picks retail's `0x7fff/0x10d1` split by itself. Same
  trap as decoding an addiu pair by eye (see the address-decoding entry above).
- To get `addu dst,<shift term>,<base>` for the first add, put a **`(char *)0 +`** in front of the offset sum:
  `*(unsigned char *)((char *)0 + (a * 384 + ((d + 0x90D0) + (int)DAT_003415a8)) + b * 64 + c * 8 + 0x3500)`.
  The plain `int` sum (`*(unsigned char *)(a * 384 + ... )`) and a pointer base (`a * 384 + (char *)(...)`) both
  reorder the add or the constant materialisation; the zero-based pointer chain is the only exact spelling found.
  The remaining `addu` pairs keep the natural `+ b*64 + c*8` order (dst = second operand).
The `p = base; return p[a*96 + b*16 + 0x3500];` two-line form that matched the smaller twin 0x0022cad0 does NOT hold
here: with three index terms the local pointer changes the first-add order (7 words differ). Converted near miss
wip/FUN_0022cb04_near.c (0x8d10 written as 0x90D0 + the zero-seeded chain) -> EXACT first compile.
## An inlined implicit POD copy brings its own null guard (2026-10-28, 0x00294088 EXACT)
The 10-byte vector append-n instance (`short v[5]` element) matched on the first real spelling once the element was left
plain POD: `struct Elem { short v[5]; };` + `new (p) Elem(x)` makes mwcc inline a **five-iteration `lh`/`sh` loop with a
`beqzl p,<skip>` guard of its own** (`li v1,5; beqzl a3,..; move a0,v1; move a2,src; move a1,dst; loop`). Adding an
`if (p)` around the construct emits that guard TWICE (one extra `beqz`, +8 bytes on the branch target, 163/161 words);
a user copy ctor (`for (i=0;i<5;i++) v[i]=o.v[i]`) unrolls into five straight `lh`/`sh` pairs instead. The 20-byte float
sibling (0x00166244) needs the opposite (explicit memberwise ctor, interleaved lwc1/swc1) — same template, different
element, so check which copy shape the element size implies before adding a ctor. Written from the 0x00166244 source with
addresses/element substituted: 161/161.
## A clamp ternary's compare direction is source-controllable (2026-10-28, 0x000adb10 EXACT)
`hi > v ? hi : v` and `v > hi ? hi : v` are the same clamp but emit `slt at,a0,v1` and `slt at,v1,a0`
respectively — mirroring the comparison flips only the two slt operands and closes a one-word park
(97/97). The parked sweep had tried `hi < v ? v : hi` (Max, wrong value) and inline helpers; the fix is
the *same value* with the comparison written from the other side. Applies to every parked "`slt` operand
order" note: rewrite the relational operator mirror-wise (`a > b` <-> `b < a`) instead of moving the arms.
## A one-off load into a local flips the compare's rs/rt (2026-10-28, 0x000dbc54 EXACT)
`if (base[i + 9] == ch) return 1;` emits `bnel a1,v0` (parameter in rs); routing the byte through
`signed char c; c = base[i + 9]; if (c == ch)` emits retail's `bnel v0,a1` (loaded byte in rs) with the
same word count — the local forces the loaded value to be the first operand slot. Neither mirroring the
`==` operands nor casting `ch` does it (both cost/skip words). Same family: `opt_strength_reduction off`
is what keeps the `addu base,i` + `lb 9(v0)` indexed form instead of a pointer walk.
## "Return the constant LAST" is what gives `blezl` + constant in the delay (2026-10-28, 0x001fb8d8 EXACT)
`int n = self->count; if (n <= 0) return 0; return self->arr[n - 1];` emits `bgtzl` over the compute plus an
extra `b` (9-10 words). Writing the zero return as the FINAL statement — `if (n > 0) return self->arr[--n]; return 0;`
— makes mwcc branch `blezl v0,<jr ra>` with `move v0,zero` in the delay slot and let the compute fall through (9/9).
The same edit fixes the address: `arr[n - 1]` folds the -1 into the load displacement (`lw 0x88`), while the
pre-decrement `arr[--n]` keeps retail's `addiu v0,v0,-1` + `lw 0x8c`. So for a "peek last element" body: guard
first, decrement the index inside the taken arm, constant return last.
## A duplicated address argument needs `opt_common_subs off` (2026-10-28, 0x000029f0 EXACT)
`F(g1, g2, &DAT, &DAT)` makes mwcc materialise the shared address once and pass `move a3,a2` (7 words, retail 9).
`#pragma opt_common_subs off` before the function restores two independent `lui`/`addiu` pairs; nothing else changes.
Same pass, same trap as the address-decoding entry: `lui 0x31; addiu -24560` is **0x30a010** (0x310000-0x5ff0), not
0x31a010 — the parked note had carried the wrong high half, which survived because the CSE diff looked identical.
## Two zero-return sites = a nested guard, not `||` (2026-10-28, 0x00050210 EXACT)
`if (i < 0 || i >= 576) return 0; return s->e[i].a;` gives the right first branch (`bltzl` + `move v0,zero`) but
collapses the second test into `slti v0` + `bnezl` and shares one zero block (8 words off). Retail's second test is
`slti at` + `beqz` landing on a SEPARATE `move v0,zero`: that is the nested guard
`if (i >= 0) { if (i < 576) return s->e[i].a; } return 0;` — 12/12 exact. Rule of thumb: count the constant-return
blocks in retail; one per written `return`, and a nested `if` keeps the outer test's `$at` branch form.
## A `char *` local forces the self-copy before a tail call's argument move (2026-10-28, 0x0014648c EXACT)
`FUN(a1, &DAT, (void *)(self + 0xd68), ...)` computes the addresses straight out of a0 and then does
`move a0,a1` — 7 words where retail has 8 with `move v0,a0` first. Introducing
`char *p = (char *)self;` and using `p + 0xd68` / `p + 0xd28` / `*(int *)(p + 0xd24)` makes mwcc copy a0 into
v0 at the top and use v0 for all three addresses (8/8). An `int *` local with word offsets (p[0x349]) is also
exact. A plain `int s = self;` local is NOT (mwcc keeps a0). C++ member/reference spellings produce the same
copy order but add a frame and `jal` instead of the tail `j`, so they are not a substitute.
## One `return -1` reached by two guards gets duplicated into one delay slot (2026-10-28, 0x001e7198 EXACT)
Two explicit `return -1;` statements make mwcc invert the FIRST guard (`bnezl` over the second load) and keep a
separate block; the exact shape is a single trailing `return -1;` reached by both tests —
`if (a != 0 && (b = *(int *)(a + 0x16c)) != 0) return *(int *)(b + 0x6c); return -1;` — which emits
`beqzl v0,<jr ra>` with `li v0,-1` in the delay and a plain `beqz` to the surviving block (11/11). An if/goto
spelling with the same single return is also exact; the assignment-in-`&&` form is the one installed.
## Store before the call: mwcc sinks it into the `jal` delay and drops the saved register (2026-10-28, 0x000f1b38 EXACT)
`FUN(self, self->f90); self->f94 = self->f90;` keeps `self` live across the call (s0 save, 17 words). Writing the
store first — `float x = self->f90; self->f94 = x; FUN(self, x);` — gives retail's 13 words: one `lwc1 f12,144(a0)`,
the `swc1 f12,148(a0)` in the jal delay, no saved register. A store moved into a call's delay slot runs before the
callee, so this reordering is legal and is what the original source did; `if (flag == 0) return;` with the same
order is also exact. Look for this whenever a draft has one extra saved register and a store after a call.
## Large memberwise copies: declare the exact member layout, write `*dst = *src` (2026-10-28, 0x001634d4 EXACT)
A 1260-byte function whose whole body is `if (dst) *dst = *src;` on a 556-byte record reproduces all 315 retail
words in ONE compile once the member layout is read off the copy sequence: `short` at 0x00, `char[16]` at 0x02
(mwcc copies an array member with a 2-byte-per-iteration loop), three single `char`s at 0x12-0x14, floats with
`int`/`short` members interleaved where the retail `lw`/`lh` occur, and sixteen SINGLE `char`s at 0x21c-0x22b
(individual char members unroll; replacing them with `char[16]` at 0x21c changes the code and breaks the match).
C++ struct assignment of a mixed float/int record uses `lwc1`/`swc1` per float, so a float-heavy copy that
looks like a hand-written field loop is often just an implicit assignment; check the accessor's stride
(0x1639c0 multiplies by 0x22c) to size the record.
## 16-byte-aligned vector locals: slot rounding and descending placement drive the frame (2026-10-28, 0x0012603c EXACT)
Declaring the helper object's float4 as `struct { float x,y,z,w; } __attribute__((aligned(16)))` (the PSP
vector type) is what produces a 384-byte frame for two helper objects and five temporaries: mwcc rounds every
16-aligned local's slot up to 16 bytes and places locals in DESCENDING address order of declaration
(a at 0xc0, d0 at 0xb0, b at 0x50 with a 0x60 slot, then d1/d2/v1/v2 at 0x40/0x30/0x20/0x10). With plain
4-aligned floats it packs at 8-byte boundaries (b at 0x58, v1 at 0x28) and the frame/offsets all shift. One
member was NOT a Vec4: the second helper's 0x44..0x54 region must stay four separate floats, because a
16-aligned Vec4 there jumps to +0x50 and grows the object past 0x58. Also: a scalar read once and used after
a block of stores (`float h = self->f80;` ... `b.f54 = h;`) is what makes retail hoist that load to the top of
the block and keep it in f3; assigning `b.f54 = self->f80;` at the store point reloads it there instead.

inline array (six calls, 12-byte elements at 0xc4), retail keeps the DESTINATION base in s2 and re-materialises it

colouring (retail a1=src/a0=dst/v1=count vs ours a2/a1/a0), a cascade that shifts every later word by one.

Across 36 flagged candidates a cast-keyed rewriter applied zero times: after a one-word drift the diff rows pair an unrelated instruction with the swc1, and the generated sources usually carry the value in an int local (`uVar3 = 0xc1800000;`) with the store made through that local, so there is no `*(undefined4 *)(base + off)` at the float offset. Converting the literal alone is worse (0x0021b088: 79/80 / 61 -> 77/80 / 62). The conversion that works changes the *store* to a float expression and, where the value is conditional, uses a float ternary - that is a per-unit source edit, not a sweep.
- 2026-10-29 (s3/s4 assignment follows the read expression, not ordering; 0x0017b554): the element/counter register split is decided by HOW the element is read, not by declaration or statement order. `elem = *p;` hoisted at the loop top compiles the element into s3 with the inner counter in s4; reading `*p` directly inside the inner loop compiles the loaded value into s4 with the counter in s3 - retail's assignment. A local read *after* the inner loop does not join that value: the inner-loop load and the late local occupy separate registers (s4 and s3), i.e. a split. The cost of the s4 form is the delete block: when the two null tests are separated by the release call, MWCC reloads for the second test, so the exact two-test shape (which needs one shared value) is lost. That trade is why the unit still parks at 15 differ with s3.
- 2026-10-29 (a retail dead duplicate is not two live tests; 0x0017b554): `beqzl s4,skip; <delay>; beqz s4,cont; nop; ...` is ONE null test whose duplicate branch targets the continuation, i.e. the second test is dead code, not a second live guard. Writing the source as nested `if (x != 0) { if (x != 0) { ... } ... }` produces a LIVE branch and costs a word (88/87, 59 differ vs 15 for the two-sequential-`if` form that reproduces the dead pair at 87/87). So: match the branch *targets*, not the branch count - a duplicate branch that lands on the continuation means one test in the source.
- 2026-10-29 (element register does not follow the load site): moving `elem = *p;` from before the inner loop to inside it (where retail's `lw s4,0(s0)` sits) leaves the element in s3 and the counter in s4 - 87/87 words, 19 differ, no assignment change. Combined with the earlier pass, the s3/s4 split follows whether the element is a hoisted local (s3) or a direct `*p` read (s4), not where the load is placed.
- 2026-10-29 (branch-target screen definitions and precision): classify from RETAIL's branch targets, not from the source. D (dead duplicate) = two conditional branches on the same register within five rows where the far skip is followed by a near skip to the continuation (`beqzl s4,0x17b608` then `beqz s4,0x17b604` on 0x0017b554); verified true there, but the rule also fires on unrelated nested conditions, so read the block before rewriting. B (materialised condition) = xor + sltiu + xori producing a register that the *next branch tests* - verified on 0x0017b554 at 0x17b5a0. S (sunk store) = a store in a branch delay slot; 38 hits, the most common pattern in the band, and it is a shape to reproduce rather than a defect to repair. Rewriting D mechanically (splitting one `if (X != 0) { call; call; }` into two sequential tests) matched none of the 37 candidates, so this screen produces candidates, not conversions.

Treat D as a locator and apply the split last, after the body matches.
